sections.title: Horner Syndrome: The Oculosympathetic Pathway Unveiled
content: First order neuron =central = posterior hypothalalmus descend uncrossed down the brain stem to terminate into ciliospinal center of budge in (intermeduolateral horn of spinal cord between C8 and T2
Second order neuron (preganglionic) pass from ciliospinal center of budge to the superiocervical ganglion in neck

Third (postganglionic) ascends along the internal carotid artery to enter the cavernous sinus where it joins the ophthalmic division of the trigeminal n then it reach ciliary body and the dilator pupillae muscle via nasociliary n and the long ciliary nerves

sections.title: Horner Syndrome: Classic Triad & Clinical Pearls

content.explanation:
P: Ptosis, A: Anisocoria (worse in dim light), M: Miosis.

Additional Clinical Pearls:
- Cluster headache
- Mugrainouscneuralgia
- Bilateral horner caused by cervical spine surgery or diabetic neuropathy

sections.title: 🚩 Painful Horner Syndrome: A Critical Red Flag!
content: Painful horner syndrome should raise the possibility of carotid dissection

sections.title: Key Examination Findings in Horner Syndrome
content: Key examination ﬁnding is that anisocoria is accentuated in dim light
Hypochromia ,heterochromia may be seen if congenital or longstanding
Mild ptosis 1-2m superiorly , slightly elevation of inferior lid (inferior ptosis ) due to weakness of inferior tarsal muscle
Reuced ipsilateral sweating if the lesion occur below superior cervical ganglion

sections.title: Differential Diagnosis of Horner Syndrome by Lesion Location

rows: Cervical spinal cord lesion, thoracic spinal cord lesion
Diabetic autonomic neuropathy, Pancoast tumour, Carotid and aortic aneurysm, Miscellaneous neck lesion (thyroid tumour, enlarged lymph nodes, trauma, postsurgical)
Internal carotid dissection, Nasopharyngeal tumour, Cavernous sinus mass, Otitis media

sections.title: Pharmacological Tests in Horner Syndrome: Confirm & Localize
sections.content:
Pharmacological tests play a crucial role in both confirming a diagnosis of Horner syndrome and localizing the lesion along the oculosympathetic pathway:
• Apraclonidine 0,5%or 1%& cocaine 4% =conﬁrm diagnosis
• Hydroxyamphetamine and adrenaline = differentiate pregaglionic from post ganglionic

sections.title: Pharmacological Tests: Detailed Mechanisms & Results
sections.content:

### Phenylephrine 1% (Dilution of 2.5% or 10% solution)
• Phenylephrine 1%: (dilution of 2,5%,or 10% solution)results: 10 days establised post ganhlionic horner pupil will dilate and ptosis temporary relieved Central or preganglionic both will not dialate. Explanation: post ganglionic lesion develop denervation hypersenditivity to adrenergic neurotransmitters due to its dysfunctional local motor nerve

• Adrenaline 0.1%: has an action similar to phenyl ephrine

### Cocaine 4%
• Cocaine 4% reseved for acute lesions or those in which apraclonidine testing is equivocal but clinical suspicion is high results :the horner pupil will not dilate( cocaine block reuptake of noradrenaline secreted at postganglionic nerve ending wich accumulate and cause dilation of normal pupil in horner syndrome there is no noradrenaline being secreated so cocaine has no effect

• Hydroxyamphitamine1%:more sensitive than phenylephrine results : postganglionic horner will not dilate Hydroxyamphetamine potentiates the release of noradrenaline from functional post ganglionic nerve endings.there is no release of noradrenaline from dysfunctional nerve

sections.title: Adie Pupil: Pathophysiology & Features (Tonic Pupil)
content: Denervation of post ganglionic parasympathetic supply to sphincter pupillae and ciliary muscle and may follow a viral illness
Occasionally AD
Sites of dysfunction: ciliary ganglion and in holmes adie syndrome dorsal root ganglion involved in reﬂex pathways
Female one eye though involvement of second eye typically develops within months or years
Symptoms: anisocoria, blurring of near vision
Signs:
- Large regular pupil
- Direct light reﬂex is absent or sluggish
- Vermiform movements of the pupillary border
- Constriction is also absent or sluggish in respone to light stomulation of the fellow eye (consensual)
- Pupil respond to near following wich redilatation is also slow
- Accomodation may manifest similar tonicity with slowed or impaired focusing for near and prolonged refocusing in the distance.
- Long standing cases may become small (holmes adies)
Clinical Pearl: Sector palsy of the iris sphincter is a hallmark sign, often best seen with slit lamp examination.

rows: Decrease lower limb deep tendon reﬂexes

sections.title: Adie Pupil: Diagnosis & Management
content: Pharmacological testing: 0,1-0,125% pilocarpine into both eyes leads to constrictions of abnormal pupil due to denervation hypersensitivity
Treatment if adies pupil:
- Reading glasses
- Sunglasses, low conc pilocarpine drops can be used for cosmetic reasons and to reduced photophopia
- Thoracic sympathectomy can be considered for excessive sweating

content: Syphilis serology should usually be checked in patient with bilateral tonic pupil

sections.title: Physiological Anisocoria
content: 1mm is present in about 20% of the normal population
Asymmetry persists to the same proportion under different levels of illumination

sections.title: Pharmacologically Mydriatic Eye
content: Does not constrict in bright light or on accomodation and there is no response to any concentration of pilocarpine

sections.title: Argyll Robertson Pupils: The 'Prostitute's Pupil'
content: Cause: neurosyphilis
Lesion: dorsal mid brain
Light near dissociation
Both pupils do not dilate well in dark
In bright light neither pupils constrict
On accomodation both constrict
After 0.1% pilocarpine neither pupil constricts distinguishing argyl robertson pupils from bilateral long standing tonic pupils
Clinical Pearl: Known as the 'Prostitute's Pupil' because it 'accommodates but does not react' (to light), a mnemonic from historical medical teaching.

sections.title: Chiasmal Visual Field Defects: An Anatomical Journey
sections.content: Visual ﬁeld defects depend on the location and direction of enlargement of compressive lesion as well as the anatomical relationship between the pituitary and chiasm.

sections.title: Chiasmal Visual Field Defects: Fiber Decussation & Lesion Correlation

rows: Bitemporal superior quadrantanopia ﬁeld loss asymmetrical
Traverse the chiasm high and posteriorly
Decussate throughout the chiasm but concentrated posteriorly
Bitemporal hemianopic changes affecting the central and paracentral ﬁelds

sections.title: Specific Chiasmal Lesions & Patterns
content: Craniopharyngioma: Anterior chiasm in conjunction with post ﬁx chiasm. Simultaneous involvement of the ﬁbres of the one optic n togeather with contralateral inferonasal ﬁbres looping forward into nerve in putative knee of wilbrand. Leads to Junctional scotoma (Central or paracentral defect on the side of optic n involvement + contralateral superotemporal defect).

sections.title: Pituitary Adenoma: Management Protocol
content: 1- Observation: silent tumour
2- Medical therapy : initial step and reduction in tumour size and secretion ( cabergoline- older promocriptin- somatostatin analogue octeriotide + supplementary hormonal correction as appropriate)
3- Surgery: transsphenoidal tumour debulking
4- Radiotherapy: sterotactic radiotherapy
5- Monitoring: serial assessment of visual function

sections.title: Wernicke Hemianopic Pupil
sections.content: Wernicke hemianopic pupil =optic tract lesion may therefore give rise to an afferent pupillary conduction defect.the pupillary light reﬂex will be normal when unaffected hemiretina is stimulated and absent when the involved hemiretina is stimulated
